_doc: Scoring weights for the content recommendation engine. These weights determine how strongly each signal influences article ranking.

personaMatch.rationale: Persona is the strongest signal because it reflects cumulative user behavior across multiple sessions. A persona match means the article's topic fundamentally aligns with the user's demonstrated interest pattern.

targetLayerMatch.rationale: Target layer (tea_lover / wellbeing / gourmet) represents the user's lifestyle segment. It is the second-strongest signal because it captures 'why' the user engages with tea content, complementing the persona 'what'.

depthMatch.rationale: Depth level (entry / explore / deep) indicates content complexity fit. It receives the lowest weight because a slightly mismatched depth is less disruptive than a wrong persona or layer — users can still benefit from adjacent depth levels.

contextTimeMatch.rationale: Time-of-day context provides a subtle relevance boost. Morning tea content is more relevant in the morning. Low weight because it is a 'nice to have' rather than a core signal.

contextSeasonMatch.rationale: Seasonal context provides a subtle relevance boost. Summer iced tea content is more relevant in summer. Low weight for the same reason as time context.

readPenalty.rationale: Small penalty for already-read articles to promote content discovery without completely hiding revisitable content.
